findings.claim: $'\n' and $'\r' ANSI-C quoting inside a bash case pattern is bash-specific and not portable to POSIX sh; ShellCheck --shell=sh flags it SC3009
findings.evidence: enable-required-check.sh lines 234: `*$'\n'*|*$'\r'*` in case pattern. Shebang is `#!/usr/bin/env bash` (line 1), which is correct; ANSI-C quoting is a bash extension and works correctly in bash. ShellCheck under --shell=bash emits no warning; under --shell=sh (or via global shellcheck.rc defaulting to sh) it would flag SC3009.
findings.impact: Zero runtime impact — script runs under bash exclusively. Risk is purely that a future lint pipeline using `shellcheck --shell=sh` or omitting `# shellcheck shell=bash` annotation would emit SC3009 noise on this line.
findings.mitigation: Add `# shellcheck shell=bash` at the top of the file (after the shebang) to suppress the portability warning and make the bash target explicit to any shell-check tooling. Alternatively, rewrite the pattern as two separate `case` arms using POSIX-compatible character matching, though that is less readable. No functional change required; this is purely a lint-hygiene nit.
